intro: A wet room is one of the most significant bathroom upgrades you can make, and in Lichfield it typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000 fully installed. That's a wide range, and the difference usually comes down to the size of the space, the condition of your existing floor structure, and the quality of finishes you choose. It's not a cheap project, but done properly a wet room adds real value to your home, looks genuinely impressive, and — especially as households age — makes daily life considerably easier. Most homeowners in Lichfield who invest in one say they wish they'd done it sooner.
localContext: Lichfield's housing stock creates some genuinely varied challenges for wet room installers. The older stone-built properties and period cottages found across the town centre and surrounding villages often have suspended timber floors, which need careful assessment before any wet room work begins. Timber floors can be adapted using a tanking system or a suitable liner, but it adds complexity and cost compared to a solid concrete slab. Modern estates on the outskirts of Lichfield tend to have ground-floor concrete bases that make installation more straightforward, though upper-floor bathrooms still require structural consideration. Lichfield also sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth factoring in when choosing your fittings and shower hardware. Limescale build-up on glass screens, tile grout, and showerheads is a genuine maintenance issue here, so many installers recommend water-resistant grout sealants and easy-clean glass coatings as standard. Specifying quality fixtures designed for hard water conditions will save you frustration in the long run.
serviceDetail: The installation process for a wet room in Lichfield generally follows the same broad stages regardless of property type, though the specifics vary. The first step is a survey of your existing bathroom — the installer needs to assess floor construction, drainage options, pipe runs, and whether the room's dimensions suit a wet room layout. For older Lichfield properties, this survey stage is particularly important and shouldn't be rushed. Once the scope is agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped back to the structural shell. The floor is then prepared and a former or linear drain is set in position to create the correct gradient — typically around 1-2% fall towards the drain. Tanking is applied to the walls and floor to create a completely watertight membrane; this is arguably the most critical part of the job and where quality really matters. Tiling or cladding is then fitted over the tanked surfaces, followed by the shower fixture, screen if required, and any additional features like a heated towel rail or underfloor heating. Plumbing and electrical work is carried out by qualified tradespeople — in Lichfield, wet room electrics must comply with Part P regulations, which requires a certified electrician for work in the bathroom zone. The whole process from strip-out to completion typically takes five to eight working days for a standard bathroom conversion.
pricing: In Lichfield, most wet room installations fall between £6,000 and £12,000 for a complete conversion including labour, waterproofing, tiling, and fixtures. A modest en-suite conversion in a newer property at the lower end of this range is realistic. A larger family bathroom in one of Lichfield's older stone-built homes — where floor remediation or structural work is needed — will push toward the upper end. Premium fittings, bespoke tile work, or the addition of underfloor heating add further cost. Underfloor heating typically adds £500–£1,200 depending on room size. Always get a written, itemised quote and check that waterproofing materials and waste alteration are explicitly included — these are where unexpected costs tend to appear.
whyLocal: Choosing a Lichfield-based installer rather than a national firm genuinely makes a difference on a project like this. Local tradespeople know the property types here — they've worked in the Victorian terraces near the Cathedral, the period cottages in the surrounding villages, and the newer builds on the town's modern estates. They understand the quirks of older Staffordshire construction and won't be caught off guard by a suspended floor or awkward pipe run. They're also easier to reach if something needs attention after the job is done. A wet room is a long-term investment, and having a local professional who stands behind their work is worth factoring into your decision.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older Lichfield property with a timber floor?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires more preparation than a concrete subfloor. A suspended timber floor needs reinforcing and a specialist liner or tanking system applied before any tiling begins. It's entirely achievable in Lichfield's older stone-built homes and period cottages — it just adds to the overall cost and timeline. Make sure your installer has specific experience with timber floor wet rooms.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Lichfield?
faqs.a: For a standard bathroom conversion, expect five to eight working days from strip-out to completion. More complex projects — particularly in older Lichfield properties where floor or drainage work is more involved — can take up to two weeks. Your installer should give you a realistic timeline at the survey stage, and it's worth asking what could extend that timeframe before work begins.

faqs.q: Does hard water in Lichfield affect how I should maintain a wet room?
faqs.a: It does. Lichfield's moderately hard water means limescale will build up on glass, tile grout, and showerheads over time. Using a squeegee after each use is the simplest habit to develop. A water softener or inline filter can reduce the problem significantly. When specifying your wet room, ask about easy-clean glass coatings and hard water-resistant grout sealants — these make a noticeable difference to long-term upkeep.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room in Lichfield?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Wet room installation is treated as permitted development for internal alterations. However, if your Lichfield property is listed — and there are several in and around the town centre — you may need listed building consent before making changes to internal fixtures or structures. Your installer should flag this, but it's worth checking with Lichfield District Council if you're unsure about your property's status.
